title: A prospective longitudinal observational study of AI-assisted analysis of perioperative voice changes and detection of postoperative vocal fold dysfunction after cervical surgery
summary:
Background:
During surgery in the neck area, the nerve that controls vocal cord movement may be injured. A laryngeal examination is currently needed to determine whether this has affected the movement of a vocal cord. This examination is invasive. We aim to establish a basis for a future non-invasive assessment using voice recordings.
Research question:
Establishment of a database of voice recordings collected before and after neck surgery, together with the corresponding laryngeal examination findings.
Methodology:
Participants record voice samples using their own device and a website before surgery and on postoperative days 1, 2 and 7. Clinicians assess vocal cord movement independently of the study using a laryngeal examination. Participants with reduced vocal cord movement provide additional weekly voice samples for 3 months.
conditions: Paralysis of vocal cords and larynx: Unilateral, complete
Paralysis of vocal cords and larynx: Unilateral, incomplete

interventions.name: Patients undergoing cervical surgery without postoperative vocal fold dysfunction will be assessed using standardised voice recordings. Vocal fold mobility will be assessed by laryngoscopy on postoperative day 2.

Patients undergoing cervical surgery with postoperative vocal fold dysfunction (reduced mobility or complete immobility of one vocal fold) will be assessed using standardised voice recordings.
